kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source's equation, quantal panel, window definition, and margin note.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the definition, the equation, the two-curve panel, and the margin warning; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The three-question reading of the quantal panel (WHAT DOES THE y-AXIS COUNT? '% of patients responding' — a QUANTAL plot, not a graded one: ED50 and TD50 are the doses at which each curve crosses 50% OF PATIENTS, not 50% of maximal effect. WHICH CURVE IS WHICH? 'Efficacy' left, 'Toxicity' right — TD50 must sit right of ED50 or the drug is unusable. WHAT SEPARATES THEM? the ED50→TD50 gap IS the therapeutic index — a wide gap (↑ TI) is safe, a narrow gap (↓ TI) is the monitoring list: warfarin, theophylline, digoxin, antiepileptic drugs, lithium) — KYP's synthesis of the page's equation, panel, and margin note into a single reading order (axis → curve identity → gap → monitoring decision).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the equation, the panel, and the margin note as parallel blocks without a unified reading protocol; the count-patients-not-effect framing and the gap-is-the-index reading are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The three KYP-original mnemonics (1 — NUMERATOR TOXIC, DENOMINATOR THERAPEUTIC: TD50 on top is the dose that harms, ED50 on the bottom is the dose that heals, so push the ratio UP for safety. 2 — QUANTAL = COUNT HEADS, NOT EFFECT: the y-axis is '% of patients responding', so ED50/TD50 are read at the 50-PATIENT line, never the 50-EFFECT line. 3 — THE LETHAL FIVE: Warfarin, Theophylline, Digoxin, Antiepileptic drugs, Lithium — the ↓ TI drugs that require frequent monitoring, named by the source's own exclamation 'Warning! These drugs are lethal!'). The page's own printed margin mnemonic 'TITE: Therapeutic Index = TD50 / ED50.' is carried VERBATIM and ATTRIBUTED to the source everywhere it appears and is NOT a KYP design.
kypExtensions.rationale: Book 233's Therapeutic index section prints exactly one mnemonic ('TITE'), which is the source's own and is attributed as such; the other three codes are KYP-original designs.

notes: Census (pdfimages + VLM): NO raster images on the page (pdfimages -list returned zero rows for pdf 255). The Therapeutic index section is typeset text plus one vector curve panel. The equation block ('Measurement of drug safety.' + TD50/ED50) and the margin mnemonic/note ('TITE' + the safer-drugs warning with the low-TI drug list + the LD50 note) print in the text layer and are carried verbatim in the note's table block and re-typeset in the registry visual's panels (ORIGINAL_KYP_ADAPTATION) — short attributed sentences, not artwork reproductions. The Efficacy/Toxicity quantal-curve panel is vector line-art in the PDF and is redrawn as an ORIGINAL_KYP_REDRAW pair of sigmoid cumulative-frequency curves in the registry visual (the standard quantal dose-response geometry of pharmacodynamics, re-drawn from scratch: '% of patients responding' vs 'Log (drug concentration)', the 50% line, ED50 and TD50 drops, and the 'Therapeutic index' gap annotation); no copyrighted artwork is reproduced. The 'TITE' mnemonic IS the source's own printed margin mnemonic (book 233) and is attributed as such in the note, the manifest, and the visual; the KYP memory layer adds three original codes (NUMERATOR TOXIC, DENOMINATOR THERAPEUTIC; QUANTAL = COUNT HEADS, NOT EFFECT; THE LETHAL FIVE). No copyrighted photographs exist on the page; nothing reproduced. EXCLUSION: the 'Receptor binding' section occupies the UPPER half of this SAME page — its header, three dose-response panels (competitive, noncompetitive, partial agonists), and AGONIST WITH table are the COMPLETED topic PH8 (receptor-binding) and are EXCLUDED from this topic: PH9 pins the same source page (pdf 255 / book 233) for its LOWER half only.
